content: Twin-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS) is a serious condition that occurs in monochorionic twin pregnancies, characterized by an imbalance in blood flow between the twins due to shared placental vessels. This condition is associated with significant risks of perinatal mortality and morbidity. Various treatment options have been developed to address TTTS, but the optimal intervention for improving maternal and fetal outcomes remains uncertain. The objective of this review was to assess the effectiveness of different treatment modalities for TTTS. The review included randomized and quasi-randomized studies comparing amnioreduction, laser coagulation, and septostomy. A systematic search was conducted, and three studies involving 253 women and 506 babies were included. The quality of the trials was judged to be moderate. Comparison of Amnioreduction and Laser Coagulation: There was no significant difference in overall mortality between amnioreduction and laser coagulation (risk ratio [RR] 0.87; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.55 to 1.38, adjusted for clustering, based on two trials). Similarly, there was no significant difference in the risk of at least one infant dying per pregnancy (RR 0.91; 95% CI 0.75 to 1.09, two trials) or the risk of both infants dying per pregnancy (RR 0.76; 95% CI 0.27 to 2.10, two trials). However, more babies in the laser coagulation group were alive without neurological abnormalities at six years of age compared to the amnioreduction group (RR 1.57; 95% CI 1.05 to 2.34, adjusted for clustering, one trial). There was no significant difference in the number of babies alive at six years with major neurological abnormalities between the two groups (RR 0.97; 95% CI 0.34 to 2.77, adjusted for clustering, one trial). The outcomes for mortality in this 2013 update differ from the 2008 update. In the earlier review, laser coagulation was associated with improved perinatal survival and reduced risk of both infants dying per pregnancy. The inclusion of the NIHCD trial in the 2013 update, which showed results in the opposite direction to the Eurofetus study (the sole laser study in the 2008 review), accounts for this discrepancy. Comparison of Amnioreduction and Septostomy: There were no significant differences in overall mortality (RR 0.83; 95% CI 0.47 to 1.47, adjusted for clustering, one trial), the risk of at least one infant dying per pregnancy (RR 0.80; 95% CI 0.48 to 1.35, one trial), or the risk of both infants dying per pregnancy (RR 0.90; 95% CI 0.37 to 2.22, one trial). There was also no significant difference in gestational age at birth between the two groups (RR 1.20; 95% CI -0.81 to 3.21, one trial). Conclusions: Endoscopic laser coagulation of anastomotic vessels remains the preferred treatment for all stages of TTTS, as it improves neurodevelopmental outcomes. However, further research is needed to evaluate the effects of treatment on milder (Quintero stages 1 and 2) and more severe (Quintero stage 4) forms of TTTS. Future studies should also focus on assessing the long-term outcomes of survivors.
